value.body: State agriculture departments recruit graduates as Agriculture Officers, Agricultural Extension Officers or Agriculture Development Officers (titles vary by state). They run farmer-facing schemes, advise on crops, seeds, fertilisers and pest management, and handle inspections, subsidies and data collection at block or district level.

items.label: Basic qualification
items.note: Some posts also accept horticulture or related degrees

items.label: Recruiting body
items.value: State PSC or subordinate services board

items.label: Bihar agriculture department posts
items.note: Includes ~866 Block Agriculture Officer posts; one state, one recruitment cycle

items.label: B.Agri enrolment
items.source: AISHE 2023-24, Ministry of Education (programme-wise enrolment, all modes)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A four-year B.Sc (Hons) Agriculture from a recognised agricultural university; some states require knowledge of the state language, and some posts have domicile rules. Apply when the state PSC or subordinate services selection board notifies posts; selection is usually a written exam on agriculture and general studies, sometimes followed by an interview.

value.title: At a glance
items: Recruitment is state-by-state and irregular; some years see no notification.
Postings are often rural, at block or district offices.
Senior posts are filled by promotion or through the state civil services exam.
Central options include ICAR's ASRB exams and the IBPS SO Agricultural Field Officer post in public-sector banks.

value.title: B.Agri enrolment in India
value.note: Based on institutions that responded to AISHE; agriculture degrees recorded under other programme names are not included.
